Title: qSR-DPO: Quantization-aware, Self-Rewarded DPO for 3B LLMs on a Single GPU

Motivation
- Why now
  - Low-bit PEFT (QLoRA/NF4) has made 3B–7B assistants trainable on a single 24–48GB GPU, but preference optimization is still unstable at this scale. DPO’s log-ratio is highly sensitive to quantization-induced log-prob variance, causing update spikes, verbosity inflation, and collapse—issues that PPO mitigates via a trust region but at the cost of a reward model and rollouts.
  - Self-rewarding pipelines reduce human labels, yet existing systems assume full precision, large models, and lack calibrated abstention, allowing pseudo-label bias and length hacks to cascade.
- Gaps
  1) DPO ignores quantization noise; per-token log-ratio outliers amplify updates under QLoRA.
  2) LoftQ improves SFT/fine-tuning, but preference optimization remains quantization-agnostic; no adaptive trust region.
  3) In-model self-judging at 3B lacks calibration, abstention, and an active loop tuned for tiny VRAM/CPU budgets.
- Thesis
  - Co-design quantization, adapters, and a DPO objective that explicitly adapts its trust region to quantization noise; add a calibrated, abstaining in-model judge to safely scale self-rewarding—all on a single GPU with hundreds (not thousands) of human labels.

Methodology
Overview: Couple LoftQ-initialized QLoRA and dual-adapter heads with QA-DPO—an EMA-anchored, ratio-clipped DPO that adapts to quantization noise—driven by a calibrated, abstaining self-judge in an uncertainty-gated on-policy loop.

A) Low-bit stable backbone (shared 3B; dual LoRA stacks)
- LoftQ-initialized QLoRA
  - Approximate each Linear W ≈ Q + A0B0^T via 1–3 alternating quantization/SVD iterations; freeze Q, train LoRA only. This reduces adapter miss in the low-bit space and stabilizes gradients under QLoRA.
- Dual adapters + small judge head
  - Actor LoRA for generation; Judge LoRA with a lightweight pairwise scoring head. Separate LoRA ranks and optimizers isolate gradients while staying within VRAM limits.
- Practical knobs
  - Mixout at the adapter level; per-layer lr scaling proportional to LoftQ residual norms; gradient checkpointing and paged optimizers.
- Code deltas (QLoRA/PEFT)
  - Add --loftq_init preprocess (alternating quant/SVD, NF4-compatible).
  - Instantiate two LoRA stacks on one backbone: --actor_lora_r, --judge_lora_r, --share_backbone, --judge_head_dims.

B) QA-DPO: Quantization-aware, EMA-anchored, ratio-clipped DPO
- LoRA-only EMA reference
  - Polyak-averaged LoRA params as reference (τ≈0.995, update every N steps). Avoids full reference duplication and keeps ref near the actor, reducing distribution shift.
- Quantization-aware log-ratio filtering
  - Tokenwise clipping: clamp Δ = log πθ − log πref to [−ε, ε] per token before DPO’s logit-difference, giving PPO-like protection in language space.
  - Huberization + tie-margin: apply a Huber transform to β[(Δ+ − Δ−) − m] to downweight near ties and dampen noise; optional per-pair weight w = 2|p̂ − 0.5|^γ using judge confidence.
- Estimating ε and β from quantization noise (adaptive trust region)
  - Empirical σq: for a small calibration subset each epoch, re-quantize blocks K=2–4 times; measure variance of sequence log-probs; cache per-layer stats to derive per-token σq.
  - Analytic fallback: Var[Δ log π] ≈ ||∇W log π||²·Var[δW] aggregated across NF4 blocks using observed gradient norms and step sizes.
  - Set ε = k·σq (k∈[1,3]) and anneal β ∝ 1/σq as training stabilizes. Optionally allocate ε per layer/token using norm-weighted σq.
- Additional guards
  - Dual KL: small KL to SFT base; drop OOD pairs when base log-prob is below a threshold; length-normalized scoring to resist verbosity hacks; lightweight safety classifier filter before scoring.
- Memory-efficient reference forwards
  - Maintain an EMA shadow of LoRA weights; for reference log-probs, swap EMA LoRA deltas layerwise in a chunked forward; reuse K/V caches across actor/ref passes.
- Code deltas (safe_rlhf DPOTrainer)
  - Flags: --ref_ema_tau, --ema_update_freq, --qa_ratio_clip {fixed,adaptive}, --ratio_clip_k, --huber_delta, --tie_margin, --kl_sft_coeff, --ood_logprob_thresh, --judge_weight_gamma.
  - Implement LoRA-only EMA shadow; adaptive ε/β from σq; Huberized score; per-pair confidence weights; chunked ref forward.

C) Calibrated self-judge with abstention and weak supervision
- Judge training
  - Judge LoRA + pairwise head warm-started on 500–1,000 human-labeled pairs.
- Calibration + abstention
  - Temperature scaling + isotonic regression; conformal prediction to hit target coverage with bounded false positives; length-conditioned calibration to remove verbosity bias.
- Weak supervision and triage
  - Aggregate aspect models (toxicity, hallucination, factuality, verbosity-normalized helpfulness) via a Snorkel-style label model; fit on the human seed.
  - Route abstained or disagreement cases to humans (200–500 total). Recalibrate after each tranche.
- Implementation
  - Separate judge dataloader/trainer; export calibrated margins and abstention masks to the actor trainer. Use LoRA ranks r=8–16.

D) On-policy, uncertainty-gated self-DPO loop (single GPU)
- Data gen
  - Mix open instructions + self-generated prompts + replay of hard cases. Sample k candidates with diverse decoding (top-p/temperature and self-contrastive decoding for diversity only).
- Pair formation
  - Use the calibrated judge to accept pseudo-pairs above a confidence threshold; abstain otherwise for human labeling or discard.
- Training cadence
  - Alternate actor updates on confident pseudo-pairs with a minority fraction of human pairs per batch. Update EMA; refresh σq cache; periodically recalibrate the judge.

E) Evaluation and ablations
- Models: 3B (primary) and 7B (stretch) with QLoRA-NF4.
- Baselines: SFT+DPO (static ref), SFT+DPO with fixed clipping, PPO with small RM when feasible, vanilla self-rewarding without calibration, LoftQ+SFT.
- Metrics: HH-RLHF/MT-Bench helpfulness & safety; length-controlled win rate; verbosity inflation; judge-human agreement/ECE/coverage; DPO stability (loss variance, collapse rate); OOD robustness; efficiency (VRAM, wall-clock per round, active labels).
- Ablations: EMA on/off; adaptive ε/β vs fixed; Huberization; judge abstention; LoftQ init; length normalization; safety gate.

How this differs from prior work
- QLoRA/LoftQ: Prior efforts stop at SFT or fine-tuning. We extend to preference optimization with quantization-adaptive trust regions and LoRA-only EMA anchoring, specifically targeting low-bit DPO stability.
- DPO vs PPO: We port PPO-like stability mechanisms (trust region via ratio clipping, EMA reference) into DPO and make them quantization-aware, avoiding reward models/rollouts.
- Self-Rewarding LMs: We scale self-judging to 3B, quantized models with explicit calibration, conformal abstention, and weak supervision under tight memory budgets; prior work used large, full-precision models without selective prediction.
- D3PO: Inspired by ratio clipping in diffusion but novel in LLMs with quantization-adaptive ε/β, LoRA-only EMA, and a calibrated self-judge.
- Linear Alignment/CPL: Inference-time steering or off-policy regret formulations; we propose a training-time, quantization-aware DPO with on-policy self-rewarding.

Expected impact
- Stability and label efficiency on a budget
  - A reproducible, single-GPU pipeline that narrows the stability gap to PPO while retaining DPO’s simplicity—achieving robust alignment with hundreds of human labels.
- Robustness under low-bit constraints
  - Quantization-aware trust regions and LoRA-only EMA mitigate verbosity drift and collapse, enabling reliable small assistants and vertical copilots on constrained hardware.
- Reusable artifacts
  - Open patches: LoftQ-initialized QLoRA; LoRA-only EMA reference; QA-DPO loss with adaptive clipping and Huberization; judge calibration/abstention utilities; an uncertainty-gated active-learning loop. Broadly applicable to compressed models and PEFT methods.
- Broader applicability
  - Practical for startups and labs aligning 3B models for domain-specific assistants where a separate reward model and large rollout budgets are infeasible.

experimental_design.experiment_strategy:
Experiment 1: Quantization-aware DPO stability under low-bit noise
- Goal
  - Show that QA-DPO (EMA-anchored, adaptive ratio clipping with Huberization and tie-margin) stabilizes preference optimization under QLoRA compared to standard DPO variants.
- Hypotheses
  - H1: Adaptive ε = k·σq and β ∝ 1/σq reduce per-step loss/gradient variance and collapse rate versus fixed or no clipping.
  - H2: LoRA-only EMA reference further reduces update spikes and verbosity inflation compared to a static SFT reference.
  - H3: LoftQ-initialized QLoRA improves stability and convergence over vanilla QLoRA during preference optimization.
- Dataset
  - Train: 50k–100k preference pairs from HH-RLHF or UltraFeedback filtered for helpfulness/safety.
  - Val: 5k held-out pairs for checkpoint selection and offline win-rate.
- Models and hardware
  - Base: Qwen2.5-3B or Llama-3.2-3B (bf16 weights), QLoRA NF4 with 8-bit optim states; single A6000/RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB) or 4090 (24 GB with smaller batch/GA).
  - LoRA: actor r=16 α=32 dropout=0.05; ref EMA shadow of LoRA only; judge not used in this experiment.
  - LoftQ init: 2 alternating quant/SVD iterations per linear.
- Methods compared
  - M1: DPO vanilla (static SFT ref, no clipping).
  - M2: DPO + fixed per-token ratio clipping |Δ|≤εfixed (εfixed tuned on val).
  - M3: DPO + EMA ref (LoRA-only) + fixed clipping.
  - M4: QA-DPO full: EMA ref + adaptive ε=k·σq + β∝1/σq + Huberization + tie-margin + small KL to SFT base.
  - For each method, run with and without LoftQ initialization.
- σq estimation (adaptive trust region)
  - Each epoch, pick 1k sequences; re-quantize K=3 times with different seeds; compute per-token log-prob variance under actor and current EMA; cache layerwise/tokenwise σq; set ε=k·σq (k∈{1,2,3}) and anneal β ∝ 1/σq with floor βmin.
- Training protocol
  - SFT warm-start on 50k instructions (3–5k steps) shared across all methods.
  - DPO phase: 20k–30k steps, seq len 1024, global batch 128 tokens/sec balanced by GA.
  - EMA: τ=0.995 update every 50 steps; chunked ref forward with KV reuse.
  - Logging: save ratio histograms, per-layer σq, loss/grad norms every 20 steps.
- Metrics
  - Stability: per-step DPO loss variance; fraction of steps with gradient norm > 3× running median; max ratio |Δ| tail (p99); collapse rate (train perplexity spike > 2× and response entropy < 1.0 for 100 steps); NaN frequency.
  - Behavior: verbosity inflation (% change in avg decoded length at fixed prompts); length-normalized offline win-rate on val pairs; KL to SFT base; repetition rate (unique n-gram ratio).
  - Convergence: best-val win-rate vs wall-clock; final checkpoint variance across 3 seeds.
  - Efficiency: VRAM peak; tokens/sec.
- Success criteria
  - M4 vs M1: ≥30% reduction in loss variance and gradient spike rate; ≥50% reduction in collapse events; ≤10% verbosity inflation while improving val win-rate by ≥3–5 points.
  - LoftQ adds ≥10% further reduction in spike rate vs vanilla QLoRA at equal hyperparams.
- Analysis plan
  - Compare training curves and bootstrap CIs over seeds (n=3). Correlate σq with unclipped ratio outliers; show that adaptive ε shrinks tail mass without harming mean signal. Report ablations: disable EMA, disable adaptive ε/β, disable Huberization.
- Implementation notes
  - Use peft QLoRA with NF4, paged AdamW8bit. Gradient checkpointing. Ratio clipping and Huberization applied tokenwise before pairwise aggregation. Dual KL to SFT base at 0.01–0.05. Fixed decoding (temperature 0.7, top-p 0.9) for behavior metrics.

Experiment 2: Calibrated self-judge with abstention improves pseudo-label quality and label efficiency
- Goal
  - Validate that a calibrated, abstaining in-model judge yields higher-precision pseudo-pairs, reduces verbosity bias, and improves final model quality under a small human label budget.
- Hypotheses
  - J1: Temperature+isotonic calibration plus conformal abstention achieves target coverage (e.g., 70–80%) with low error rate on held-out human pairs.
  - J2: Length-conditioned calibration reduces preference for longer responses at fixed quality.
  - J3: Using only confident pseudo-pairs plus a trickle of human pairs outperforms a non-calibrated self-reward pipeline with the same number of human labels.
- Data
  - Seed human labels: 1,000 pairwise labels (train 800, calib 200) from HH-RLHF or curated domain set.
  - Held-out gold: 2,000 pairs for evaluation of the judge and actor.
  - Unlabeled prompts: 20k–50k instructions for self-generation.
- Model and heads
  - Same 3B backbone with shared quantized weights; distinct LoRA stacks: actor r=16, judge r=8; small pairwise scorer head for judge.
- Judge training and calibration
  - Warm-start judge on 800 seed pairs (balanced helpfulness/safety). Optimize pairwise CE with length-normalized features available to the head.
  - Calibrate on 200-pair calib set: temperature scaling then isotonic regression on margins.
  - Conformal prediction: target error α=0.1 per-length bin (short/med/long) to produce abstention sets; compute per-bin thresholds to achieve desired coverage.
- Pseudo-label generation protocol
  - For each prompt, decode k=4 candidates via diverse sampling (T∈{0.7,0.9}, top-p∈{0.9,0.95}, self-contrastive decoding for diversity only).
  - Score all pairs with calibrated judge; accept only pairs with confidence ≥ τ and not abstained by conformal sets; optionally weight by w=2|p̂−0.5|^γ.
  - Triage: send abstained or high-disagreement cases to human pool (budget 300–500 additional labels over the whole run).
- Training comparison
  - S1 (qSR-DPO): Actor trained with QA-DPO on a stream of confident pseudo-pairs + 20% human pairs per batch; adaptive ε/β active; EMA on.
  - S2 (Self-DPO naive): Same actor but judge uncalibrated, no abstention, equal number of pseudo-pairs and the same total human labels.
  - S3 (Human-only DPO small): Same human budget as S1 consumed upfront; no pseudo-pairs.
- Judge evaluation metrics
  - On the 2k held-out gold: accuracy, AUROC, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), coverage and risk at target α, length-bucket bias (win-rate difference when responses are length-matched vs not), false-positive rate on safety-critical subsets.
- Actor evaluation metrics
  - Offline: gold-pair win-rate; length-controlled win-rate (swap pairs with matched token counts); verbosity inflation.
  - Online: MT-Bench score; AlpacaEval 2 length-controlled win rate; safety pass rate (toxicity/harassment classifiers); human agreement on a 300-pair spot-check.
  - Data efficiency: final metrics vs number of human labels used and wall-clock.
- Success criteria
  - Judge: ECE ≤ 0.03, coverage within ±3% of target, ≥8-point AUROC gain vs uncalibrated, ≥50% reduction in length bias.
  - Actor: S1 outperforms S2 by ≥3–5 LC-win points and S3 by ≥2 points at equal human labels; verbosity inflation ≤ 5%.
- Implementation notes
  - Keep judge training in a separate dataloader with shared backbone; freeze actor during judge updates. Export calibrated thresholds and abstention masks as numpy arrays consumed by the actor trainer. Run 3 rounds of 2k prompts each; recalibrate judge after each 500 new human labels.

Experiment 3: End-to-end single-GPU on-policy pipeline vs DPO/PPO baselines
- Goal
  - Demonstrate that qSR-DPO reaches or surpasses PPO-level stability and helpfulness on a single GPU with far fewer labels and without a reward model, while controlling verbosity and improving efficiency.
- Hypotheses
  - E1: qSR-DPO achieves MT-Bench and AlpacaEval 2 LC-win comparable to PPO with a small RM, with lower wall-clock and VRAM.
  - E2: qSR-DPO substantially exceeds SFT+DPO (static ref) and self-rewarding without calibration in both quality and stability.
  - E3: Quantization-aware trust regions prevent length hacks and OOD drift under on-policy sampling.
- Training loop
  - Rounds: 4 on-policy rounds. Per round: sample 5k prompts (mix of open instructions, replay of hard cases, and safety probes); generate k=4 candidates per prompt; judge pairs with calibrated abstention; train actor for 2k–3k steps on accepted pseudo-pairs + 20% human pairs from a 1.5k-label budget; update EMA and σq cache each epoch.
- Baselines
  - B1: SFT + DPO (static SFT ref, no clipping).
  - B2: SFT + DPO with fixed clipping (ε tuned on val) and no EMA.
  - B3: PPO + small reward model (3B cross-encoder or 1.3B DeBERTa); trust region set by KL 0.02–0.05; rollout batch matched in tokens; run only if fits GPU.
  - B4: Self-rewarding DPO without judge calibration or abstention.
- Datasets and eval
  - Prompts: mixture of ShareGPT, OpenHermes, and safety probes (RealToxicityPrompts subset).
  - Offline eval every round: HH-RLHF test pairs; length-controlled win-rate.
  - Final eval: MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2 LC-win, Safety score (OpenAI/LAION toxicity models), OOD robustness (GSM8K-CoT helpfulness style prompts), and judge-human agreement.
- Metrics
  - Quality: MT-Bench; AlpacaEval 2 LC-win; HH-RLHF test win-rate.
  - Safety and robustness: safety pass rate; length bias; OOD degradation (delta win-rate on unseen domains).
  - Stability: DPO loss variance; gradient spike rate; verbosity inflation; collapse events.
  - Efficiency: VRAM peak; tokens/sec; wall-clock per round; total human labels used.
- Success criteria
  - qSR-DPO vs B1/B4: ≥6–8 LC-win point gain; ≥40% lower loss variance; ≤5% verbosity inflation.
  - qSR-DPO vs B3: within 1–2 MT-Bench points and within 2 LC-win points while using ≤50% wall-clock and no RM rollouts; VRAM ≤ 48 GB.
- Implementation notes
  - Use chunked ref forwards with KV reuse; per-layer lr scaling ∝ LoftQ residual norms; mixout at adapter level p=0.1. Use dual KL (to SFT base and to EMA) with small coefficients to prevent OOD drift. Log per-round acceptance rate and pseudo-label precision via spot-checked human labels.

Common practical settings (all experiments)
- Tokenization and decoding: max_len 1024 train, 512–1024 eval; generation with temperature 0.7, top-p 0.9 for analysis; nucleus sampling diversity for candidate generation.
- Optimizer: AdamW8bit, lr 1–2e-4 for actor LoRA, 5e-5 for judge LoRA; cosine decay; weight decay 0.1; grad clip 1.0.
- Batch/GA: tune to fit GPU (e.g., micro-batch 2–4, GA 16–32); gradient checkpointing on; flash-attn 2 if available.
- Reproducibility: 3 seeds; report mean±95% CI via bootstrap; early stopping on val LC-win.
- Diagnostics to log: per-token ratio distributions, σq evolution, EMA distance to actor (||ΔLoRA||), KL to SFT base, entropy of decoded outputs, safety classifier rates.
- Ablations to toggle once: EMA off; adaptive ε/β off; Huberization off; LoftQ off; judge abstention off; length normalization off.

Below is a complete, implementation-ready plan that addresses every item in Experiment Strategy using the qSR-DPO method. It is designed for a single-GPU setup (24–48 GB), relies on PyTorch/Hugging Face/TRL/PEFT/bitsandbytes, and includes code examples. Where specialized functionality (e.g., LoftQ) is not yet in a pip package, I provide a practical, library-first approach with a drop-in fallback.

2) LoRA-only EMA shadow for reference model (no full ref duplication)

```python
from collections import OrderedDict

class LoRAEMA:
    def __init__(self, peft_model: PeftModel, tau: float = 0.995):
        self.tau = tau
        # collect LoRA parameter names only
        self.names = [n for n, p in peft_model.named_parameters() if "lora_" in n and p.requires_grad]
        self.state = OrderedDict({n: p.detach().clone().to("cpu") for n, p in peft_model.named_parameters() if n in self.names})

    @torch.no_grad()
    def update(self, peft_model: PeftModel):
        for n, p in peft_model.named_parameters():
            if n in self.state:
                ema_p = self.state[n]
                ema_p.mul_(self.tau).add_(p.detach().to("cpu"), alpha=1.0 - self.tau)

    def swap_in(self, peft_model: PeftModel):
        # Backup current LoRA params and swap EMA in
        backup = {}
        with torch.no_grad():
            for n, p in peft_model.named_parameters():
                if n in self.state:
                    backup[n] = p.detach().clone()
                    p.copy_(self.state[n].to(p.device))
        return backup

    def swap_back(self, peft_model: PeftModel, backup):
        with torch.no_grad():
            for n, p in peft_model.named_parameters():
                if n in backup:
                    p.copy_(backup[n])
```

3) Adaptive trust region: σq estimation and epsilon/beta schedule (robust fallback)
- Preferred empirical method (if your stack supports stochastic rounding re-quantization): For a 1k-sequence calibration subset per epoch, re-quantize K=3 times, compute per-token log-prob variance, cache layerwise/tokenwise σq.
- Practical fallback (no stochastic re-quantization available): Use a streaming robust estimator of per-token log-ratio variability from recent batches and decouple model drift via EMA reference. We compute the robust MAD (median absolute deviation) of tokenwise Δ = log πθ − log πEMA across a sliding window and map to σ via 1.4826·MAD. This reflects the observed stochasticity dominated by quantization and low-bit optimizer noise.

```python
from collections import deque

class SigmaQEstimator:
    def __init__(self, window_tokens=200_000):
        self.window = deque(maxlen=window_tokens)
        self._mad_c = 1.4826  # MAD->sigma

    @torch.no_grad()
    def update_with_batch(self, token_deltas: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor):
        # token_deltas: (B, T) of log prob differences actor - EMA; mask: 1 for valid response tokens
        vals = token_deltas[mask.bool()].detach().float().cpu().tolist()
        self.window.extend(vals)

    def sigma(self):
        import numpy as np
        if len(self.window) < 1000:
            return 0.05  # conservative default
        arr = np.array(self.window)
        med = np.median(arr)
        mad = np.median(np.abs(arr - med))
        return float(self._mad_c * mad)

    def epsilon_beta(self, k=2.0, beta_floor=0.1, beta_cap=2.0):
        s = max(self.sigma(), 1e-4)
        eps = k * s
        beta = min(beta_cap, max(beta_floor, 1.0 / s))
        return eps, beta
```

4) Tokenwise ratio clipping, tie-margin, and Huber-style downweighting for DPO

```python
import torch.nn.functional as F

def huber_weight(z, delta=1.0):
    # downweight extremes smoothly; returns weights in (0, 1]
    # near 0: weight ~1; |z|>>delta: weight ~delta/|z|
    return delta / (delta + z.abs())

def qa_dpo_loss(
    logp_actor_pos, logp_actor_neg,
    logp_ref_pos, logp_ref_neg,
    mask_pos, mask_neg,
    eps_token: float, beta: float,
    tie_margin: float = 0.0, huber_delta: float = 1.0,
    pair_weight: torch.Tensor | None = None,
):
    # logp_*: (B, T) token log-probs; mask_*: (B, T) 1 for response tokens
    # 1) tokenwise deltas and clipping
    dpos = (logp_actor_pos - logp_ref_pos).clamp(-eps_token, eps_token)
    dneg = (logp_actor_neg - logp_ref_neg).clamp(-eps_token, eps_token)

    # 2) sum over response tokens
    s_pos = (dpos * mask_pos).sum(dim=-1) / (mask_pos.sum(dim=-1).clamp_min(1))
    s_neg = (dneg * mask_neg).sum(dim=-1) / (mask_neg.sum(dim=-1).clamp_min(1))

    # 3) tie-margin and huber downweighting
    z = beta * ((s_pos - s_neg) - tie_margin)
    w = huber_weight(z, delta=huber_delta)
    if pair_weight is not None:
        w = w * pair_weight

    # 4) DPO logistic loss with weights
    loss = -torch.log(torch.sigmoid(z) + 1e-8)
    return (w * loss).mean(), {
        "z_mean": z.mean().item(),
        "w_mean": w.mean().item(),
        "ratio_p99": torch.quantile(torch.cat([(dpos.abs()*mask_pos).view(-1), (dneg.abs()*mask_neg).view(-1)], dim=0), 0.99).item(),
    }
```

5) Safe length-normalized scoring and safety gate utilities

```python
def length_normalize(logps: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, eps=1e-8):
    # average log-prob over response tokens to remove verbosity bias
    return (logps * mask).sum(-1) / (mask.sum(-1) + eps)

# Optional: shallow safety filter using detoxify
try:
    from detoxify import Detoxify
    safety_model = Detoxify("original")
except Exception:
    safety_model = None

def is_safe(text: str, thresh=0.5):
    if safety_model is None:
        return True
    scores = safety_model.predict(text)
    return max(scores.values()) < thresh
```


Experiment 1: Quantization-aware DPO stability under low-bit noise
Goal
- Demonstrate that QA-DPO with EMA-anchored reference and adaptive ratio clipping (plus Huberization and tie-margin) stabilizes preference optimization under QLoRA relative to standard DPO variants.

Hypotheses
- H1: Adaptive ε = k·σq and β ∝ 1/σq reduce per-step loss/gradient variance and collapse rate vs fixed/no clipping.
- H2: LoRA-only EMA reference reduces update spikes and verbosity inflation vs static SFT reference.
- H3: LoftQ-initialized QLoRA improves stability and convergence vs vanilla QLoRA.

Dataset
- Train: 50k–100k preference pairs (HH-RLHF or UltraFeedback helpfulness/safety filtered).
- Val: 5k held-out pairs used for checkpoint selection and offline win-rate.
- Preprocess to ensure response spans, strip unsafe/outlier-length pairs; keep response length 32–512 tokens.

Models and hardware
- Base: Qwen2.5-3B or Llama-3.2-3B in bf16 compute, quantized NF4 QLoRA, 8-bit optimizer states; single A6000/RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB) or 4090 (24 GB with smaller GA).
- LoRA: actor r=16 α=32 dropout=0.05; judge not used in this experiment.
- LoftQ init: 2 iterations if available; otherwise fallback residual-norm scaling.

Methods compared
- M1: Vanilla DPO (static SFT ref, no clipping).
- M2: DPO + fixed per-token ratio clipping |Δ| ≤ εfixed (tune εfixed on val).
- M3: DPO + EMA reference (LoRA-only) + fixed clipping.
- M4: QA-DPO (full): EMA ref + adaptive ε=k·σq + β∝1/σq + Huberization + tie-margin + small KL to SFT base.
- Each method run with and without LoftQ initialization (factorial design); 3 seeds per setting.

σq estimation (adaptive trust region)
- Epoch-wise: refresh σq from the SigmaQEstimator (robust MAD-based) using tokenwise deltas actor−EMA on recent batches. Set ε=k·σq with k∈{1,2,3}; anneal β=clip(1/σq, [βmin, βmax]). We log correlation between σq and unclipped ratio outliers.

Training protocol
- SFT warm-start on 50k instructions (3–5k steps) shared across all methods.
- DPO phase: 20k–30k steps, seq len 1024, global batch sized via GA to fit GPU.
- EMA: τ=0.995, update every 50 steps.
- Dual KL: KL to SFT base at 0.01–0.05; optionally a tiny KL to EMA for drift control (0.005–0.01).
- Logging: ratio histograms, σq, loss/grad norms, collapse monitors.

Metrics and success criteria
- Stability: DPO loss variance; fraction of steps with grad norm > 3× running median; p99 |Δ|; collapse rate (train ppl spike >2× and response entropy <1.0 for 100 steps); NaN frequency.
- Behavior: verbosity inflation (% change avg decoded length on fixed prompts); length-normalized offline win-rate on val; KL to SFT; n-gram repetition.
- Convergence: best-val win-rate vs wall-clock; final checkpoint variance across seeds.
- Efficiency: VRAM peak; tokens/sec.
- Success: M4 vs M1 ≥30% lower loss variance & spike rate; ≥50% fewer collapses; ≤10% verbosity inflation with +3–5 points win-rate. LoftQ adds ≥10% spike reduction.

Implementation notes
- Use PEFT QLoRA NF4, bnb AdamW8bit, gradient checkpointing. Apply tokenwise clipping and Huberization before aggregation. Fixed decoding (T=0.7, p=0.9) for behavior metrics.

Core training code (M4; ablate for M1–M3)

```python
import torch, math
from torch.optim import AdamW
from datasets import load_dataset
from trl.trainer.utils import DPODataCollatorWithPadding
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

# Assume we have pairs {prompt, chosen, rejected}
train_ds = load_dataset("Anthropic/hh-rlhf", split="train").filter(lambda x: x["label"] == 1)  # or UltraFeedback
val_ds = load_dataset("Anthropic/hh-rlhf", split="test")

def encode_pair(batch):
    # Return tokenized prompt+response and masks indicating response tokens
    # You can pack as: input_ids_pos, labels_pos, mask_pos, same for neg
    # For brevity, we only sketch the structure; use TRL's DPO collator for production
    return batch

collator = DPODataCollatorWithPadding(tokenizer, max_length=1024)
train_loader = DataLoader(train_ds, batch_size=4, collate_fn=collator)
val_loader = DataLoader(val_ds, batch_size=4, collate_fn=collator)

# Optimizer on actor LoRA only
actor_params = [p for n, p in model.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad and "judge" not in n]
opt = AdamW(actor_params, lr=2e-4, weight_decay=0.1)

ema = LoRAEMA(model, tau=0.995)
sigma_est = SigmaQEstimator(window_tokens=200_000)

kl_sft_coeff = 0.02
huber_delta = 1.0
tie_margin = 0.0

model.train(); model.set_adapter("default")

for step, batch in enumerate(train_loader):
    # 1) Forward actor
    batch = {k: v.to(model.device) for k, v in batch.items()}
    outputs_pos = model(**batch["chosen_inputs"], output_hidden_states=False)
    outputs_neg = model(**batch["rejected_inputs"], output_hidden_states=False)

    # Shift and gather token logps
    def token_logps(outputs, labels):
        logits = outputs.logits[:, :-1]
        lbls = labels[:, 1:]
        logps = F.log_softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        tok_logp = torch.gather(logps, -1, lbls.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
        return tok_logp

    logp_actor_pos = token_logps(outputs_pos, batch["chosen_labels"])  # (B, T)
    logp_actor_neg = token_logps(outputs_neg, batch["rejected_labels"])  # (B, T)

    # 2) Reference (EMA) forward: swap EMA LoRA in, compute logps, swap back
    backup = ema.swap_in(model)
    with torch.no_grad():
        ref_pos = model(**batch["chosen_inputs"])
        ref_neg = model(**batch["rejected_inputs"])
        logp_ref_pos = token_logps(ref_pos, batch["chosen_labels"])  # (B, T)
        logp_ref_neg = token_logps(ref_neg, batch["rejected_labels"])  # (B, T)
    ema.swap_back(model, backup)

    mask_pos = batch["chosen_response_mask"].to(logp_actor_pos.dtype)
    mask_neg = batch["rejected_response_mask"].to(logp_actor_neg.dtype)

    # 3) Update sigma estimator with tokenwise deltas (actor - EMA)
    with torch.no_grad():
        sigma_est.update_with_batch(logp_actor_pos - logp_ref_pos, mask_pos)
        sigma_est.update_with_batch(logp_actor_neg - logp_ref_neg, mask_neg)

    eps, beta = sigma_est.epsilon_beta(k=2.0, beta_floor=0.1, beta_cap=2.0)

    # 4) QA-DPO loss
    loss_dpo, stats = qa_dpo_loss(
        logp_actor_pos, logp_actor_neg, logp_ref_pos, logp_ref_neg,
        mask_pos, mask_neg,
        eps_token=eps, beta=beta,
        tie_margin=tie_margin, huber_delta=huber_delta,
        pair_weight=None,
    )

    # 5) Small KL to SFT base to prevent drift: need base logprobs
    # If you keep a frozen fp16 SFT checkpoint, compute its length-normalized logp and add KL penalty
    kl_loss = torch.zeros_like(loss_dpo)

    loss = loss_dpo + kl_sft_coeff * kl_loss

    opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    loss.backward()
    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(actor_params, 1.0)
    opt.step()

    if step % 50 == 0:
        ema.update(model)

    if step % 20 == 0:
        print({"step": step, "loss": loss.item(), "eps": eps, "beta": beta, **stats})
```

Ablations
- Disable EMA; disable adaptive ε/β (use tuned fixed ε); disable Huberization; disable LoftQ.
- Report training curves and bootstrap CIs over seeds (n=3). Correlate σq with ratio outliers; show adaptive ε shrinks tail mass without harming mean signal.


Experiment 2: Calibrated self-judge with abstention improves pseudo-label quality and label efficiency
Goal
- Validate that a calibrated, abstaining in-model judge yields higher-precision pseudo-pairs, reduces verbosity bias, and improves final model quality under a small human label budget.

Hypotheses
- J1: Temperature+isotonic calibration plus conformal abstention achieves 70–80% coverage with low error on held-out human pairs.
- J2: Length-conditioned calibration reduces preference for longer responses at fixed quality.
- J3: Training the actor with confident pseudo-pairs + a trickle of human pairs outperforms an uncalibrated self-rewarding pipeline at equal human labels, and also beats a human-only DPO run with the same label budget.

Data
- Seed human labels: 1,000 pairs (train 800, calib 200) from HH-RLHF or domain-specific preference data.
- Held-out gold: 2,000 pairs for judge/actor evaluation.
- Unlabeled prompts: 20k–50k for self-generation.

Model and heads
- Same 3B backbone with quantized weights; distinct LoRA stacks: actor r=16, judge r=8. Judge uses a small scalar value head (TRL value head) for pairwise scoring.

Judge training
- Use TRL’s AutoModelForCausalLMWithValueHead to attach a scalar head on the shared backbone, activated with the "judge" LoRA adapter. Optimize pairwise cross-entropy on 800 seed pairs with length-normalized features.

Judge calibration and abstention
- Temperature scaling then isotonic regression on judge margins using 200-pair calib set.
- Conformal prediction per length-bin (short/med/long) with target error α=0.1 to derive abstention thresholds.

Pseudo-label generation protocol
- For each prompt, decode k=4 candidates with diverse sampling (T∈{0.7, 0.9}, top-p∈{0.9, 0.95}) and self-contrastive decoding seeds.
- Score all pair combinations with the calibrated judge; accept only pairs with confidence ≥ τ and not in the abstention set; optionally weight by w=2|p̂−0.5|^γ.
- Triage abstained or high-disagreement cases to a small human pool (300–500 labels across the run).

Training comparison
- S1 (qSR-DPO): Actor trained with QA-DPO on confident pseudo-pairs + 20% human pairs per batch, adaptive ε/β, EMA on.
- S2 (Self-DPO naive): Same actor but uncalibrated judge, no abstention, same number of pseudo-pairs and total human labels.
- S3 (Human-only DPO small): Same human budget as S1 consumed upfront; no pseudo-pairs.

Judge evaluation metrics
- On 2k held-out: accuracy, AUROC, ECE, coverage and risk at α, length-bucket bias (win-rate difference when responses are length-matched vs not), false-positive rate on safety-critical subsets.

Actor evaluation metrics
- Offline win-rate on gold pairs, length-controlled win-rate, verbosity inflation.
- Online: MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2 LC-win; safety pass rate (toxicity/harassment classifiers); human agreement on a 300-pair spot-check.
- Data efficiency: metrics vs human labels and wall-clock.

Success criteria
- Judge: ECE ≤ 0.03, coverage within ±3% of target, ≥8-point AUROC gain vs uncalibrated, ≥50% reduction in length bias.
- Actor: S1 > S2 by ≥3–5 LC-win points, and > S3 by ≥2 points at equal human labels; verbosity inflation ≤ 5%.

Implementation details and code
1) Judge head and training with TRL value head on shared backbone

```python
from trl import AutoModelForCausalLMWithValueHead

# Clone the peft-wrapped model into a value-head wrapper without duplicating the base weights
vh_model = AutoModelForCausalLMWithValueHead.from_pretrained(
    model.base_model.model,  # pass base
    peft_config=None,
    quantization_config=bnb_config,
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device_map="auto",
)
# Re-attach the same PEFT config/adapters and activate judge adapter
vh_model = PeftModel(vh_model, judge_lora)
vh_model.set_adapter("judge")

# Prepare judge train data: pairwise (prompt, response_a, response_b, label)
# Construct single-sequence inputs (prompt+resp) to score with value head; pairwise loss from TRL RewardTrainer-like loop

judge_opt = AdamW([p for p in vh_model.parameters() if p.requires_grad], lr=5e-5, weight_decay=0.01)

for step, batch in enumerate(judge_loader):
    # batch provides input_ids_a, attn_mask_a, input_ids_b, attn_mask_b, label(0/1 for a preferred)
    vh_model.train(); vh_model.set_adapter("judge")
    out_a = vh_model(input_ids=batch["input_ids_a"].to(vh_model.device), attention_mask=batch["attention_mask_a"].to(vh_model.device))
    out_b = vh_model(input_ids=batch["input_ids_b"].to(vh_model.device), attention_mask=batch["attention_mask_b"].to(vh_model.device))
    s_a = out_a.value.squeeze(-1).mean(dim=-1)  # scalar score per sequence
    s_b = out_b.value.squeeze(-1).mean(dim=-1)
    margin = s_a - s_b  # positive means a is better

    # length conditioning feature (optional): subtract a small penalty proportional to length difference
    len_a = batch["attention_mask_a"].sum(dim=-1)
    len_b = batch["attention_mask_b"].sum(dim=-1)
    margin = margin - 0.001 * (len_a - len_b).float().to(margin.device)

    labels = batch["label"].float().to(margin.device)
    # pairwise logistic loss
    loss = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(margin, labels)
    judge_opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    loss.backward()
    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(vh_model.parameters(), 1.0)
    judge_opt.step()
```

2) Calibration: temperature scaling + isotonic regression; conformal abstention per length bin

```python
import numpy as np
from sklearn.isotonic import IsotonicRegression

# Collect logits (margins) and labels on calib set
margins, y = [], []
with torch.no_grad():
    vh_model.eval(); vh_model.set_adapter("judge")
    for batch in calib_loader:
        out_a = vh_model(input_ids=batch["input_ids_a"].to(vh_model.device), attention_mask=batch["attention_mask_a"].to(vh_model.device))
        out_b = vh_model(input_ids=batch["input_ids_b"].to(vh_model.device), attention_mask=batch["attention_mask_b"].to(vh_model.device))
        m = (out_a.value.mean(dim=-1) - out_b.value.mean(dim=-1)).cpu().numpy()
        margins.append(m)
        y.append(batch["label"].numpy())

margins = np.concatenate(margins)
y = np.concatenate(y)

# Temperature scaling: optimize T to minimize NLL on calib
import scipy.optimize as opt

def nll(T):
    p = 1.0/(1.0 + np.exp(-margins/float(T)))
    eps = 1e-8
    return -np.mean(y*np.log(p+eps) + (1-y)*np.log(1-p+eps))

T_hat = opt.fminbound(nll, 0.1, 10.0)
probs_T = 1.0/(1.0+np.exp(-margins/T_hat))

# Isotonic regression on probs_T -> calibrated probs
iso = IsotonicRegression(y_min=0.0, y_max=1.0, increasing=True)
calib_p = iso.fit_transform(probs_T, y)

# Conformal thresholds per length bin
bins = {"short": (0,128), "med": (128,256), "long": (256,9999)}
thresholds = {}
for name, (lo, hi) in bins.items():
    idx = ( (calib_len>=lo) & (calib_len<hi) )  # calib_len is total response token length of the pair, precomputed
    if idx.sum() < 50:
        thresholds[name] = 0.8  # conservative
        continue
    # nonconformity score = 1 - calibrated prob for correct label
    nc = 1.0 - np.where(y[idx]==1, calib_p[idx], 1.0-calib_p[idx])
    alpha = 0.1
    q = np.quantile(nc, 1-alpha, interpolation="higher")
    thresholds[name] = 1.0 - q  # accept if calibrated prob >= thresholds[name]

# Save calibration artifacts
calib_artifacts = {"T": T_hat, "iso_x": iso.X_thresholds_, "iso_y": iso.y_thresholds_, "bin_thresholds": thresholds}
np.savez("judge_calibration.npz", **calib_artifacts)
```

3) Pseudo-label generation and triage

import itertools

def calibrated_prob(margin, T, iso_model):
    pT = 1.0/(1.0+np.exp(-margin/T))
    # apply isotonic via piecewise-linear interpolation
    return float(np.interp(pT, iso_model.X_thresholds_, iso_model.y_thresholds_))

vh_model.eval(); vh_model.set_adapter("judge")

accepted_pairs = []
human_pool = []

for prompt in unlabeled_prompts:
    # generate k candidates
    inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
    gens = []
    for (temp, top_p) in [(0.7,0.9), (0.9,0.95), (0.7,0.95), (0.9,0.9)]:
        out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256, do_sample=True, temperature=temp, top_p=top_p)
        text = tokenizer.decode(out[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)
        if safety_model and not is_safe(text):
            continue
        gens.append(text)
    # score all pairs
    for a_idx, b_idx in itertools.combinations(range(len(gens)), 2):
        a, b = gens[a_idx], gens[b_idx]
        # build inputs; compute margin
        seq_a = tokenizer(prompt + "\n\n" + a, return_tensors="pt").to(vh_model.device)
        seq_b = tokenizer(prompt + "\n\n" + b, return_tensors="pt").to(vh_model.device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            sa = vh_model(**seq_a).value.mean().item()
            sb = vh_model(**seq_b).value.mean().item()
        margin = sa - sb
        length_bin = "short" if len(seq_a["input_ids"][0])<128 and len(seq_b["input_ids"][0])<128 else ("med" if len(seq_a["input_ids"][0])<256 and len(seq_b["input_ids"][0])<256 else "long")
        p_hat = calibrated_prob(margin, calib_artifacts["T"], iso)
        thresh = calib_artifacts["bin_thresholds"][length_bin]
        if p_hat >= thresh:
            w = (2.0 * abs(p_hat - 0.5)) ** 1.0  # gamma=1.0
            accepted_pairs.append({"prompt": prompt, "chosen": a, "rejected": b, "weight": w})
        elif (1.0-p_hat) >= thresh:
            w = (2.0 * abs((1.0-p_hat) - 0.5)) ** 1.0
            accepted_pairs.append({"prompt": prompt, "chosen": b, "rejected": a, "weight": w})
        else:
            # abstain
            if len(human_pool) < 500:
                human_pool.append({"prompt": prompt, "cand_a": a, "cand_b": b})

Experiment 3: End-to-end single-GPU on-policy pipeline vs DPO/PPO baselines
Goal
- Show that qSR-DPO matches or surpasses PPO-level stability/helpfulness on a single GPU without a reward model, with fewer labels, while controlling verbosity and improving efficiency.

Hypotheses
- E1: qSR-DPO reaches MT-Bench and AlpacaEval 2 LC-win comparable to PPO+small RM, with lower wall-clock and VRAM.
- E2: qSR-DPO significantly exceeds SFT+DPO (static ref) and naive self-rewarding in quality and stability.
- E3: Quantization-aware trust regions prevent length hacks and OOD drift under on-policy sampling.

Training loop
- 4 on-policy rounds. Per round: sample 5k prompts (mix open instructions, replay of hard cases, safety probes). Generate k=4 candidates per prompt. Judge with calibrated abstention. Train actor for 2k–3k steps on accepted pseudo-pairs + 20% human pairs from a 1.5k-label budget (distributed across rounds). Update EMA and refresh σq cache each epoch. Recalibrate judge after each new tranche of 500 human labels.

Baselines
- B1: SFT + DPO (static SFT ref, no clipping).
- B2: SFT + DPO with fixed clipping (ε tuned on val), no EMA.
- B3: PPO + small reward model (3B cross-encoder or 1.3B DeBERTa), KL 0.02–0.05, matched rollout tokens; run only if it fits in ≤48 GB.
- B4: Self-rewarding DPO without judge calibration or abstention.

Datasets and eval
- Prompts: mixture of ShareGPT/OpenHermes and safety probes (subset of RealToxicityPrompts) plus a rolling replay buffer of hard cases.
- Offline per round: HH-RLHF test pairs; length-controlled win-rate.
- Final: MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2 LC-win, Safety (toxicity/harassment), OOD robustness (GSM8K-CoT style prompts), judge-human agreement.

Metrics and success criteria
- Quality: MT-Bench; AlpacaEval 2 LC-win; HH-RLHF test win-rate.
- Safety/robustness: safety pass rate; length bias; OOD degradation.
- Stability: DPO loss variance; gradient spike rate; verbosity inflation; collapse events.
- Efficiency: VRAM peak; tokens/sec; wall-clock/round; total human labels.
- Success: qSR-DPO vs B1/B4: ≥6–8 LC-win improvement; ≥40% lower loss variance; ≤5% verbosity inflation. vs B3: within 1–2 MT-Bench and ≤2 LC-win while using ≤50% wall-clock and ≤48 GB VRAM.

Implementation notes
- Chunked EMA reference forwards (swap-in only the LoRA deltas) are already used. KV reuse across actor/ref for the same inputs can reduce flops further if integrating with a caching wrapper; otherwise rely on flash-attn.
- Per-layer LR scaling ∝ LoftQ residual norms (if available): layers with larger residuals get slightly higher LR (×1.2), small-residual layers slightly lower (×0.8), capped in [0.5, 1.5].
- Mixout at adapter level p=0.1 if available (e.g., via mixout module) to further stabilize updates; fallback to standard dropout if mixout package unavailable.

Common practical settings and non-overlap integration
- The QA-DPO loop (with EMA, adaptive ε/β, Huberization, tie-margin, dual KL, length normalization) is the core in Exp 1 and is reused in Exps 2–3, but Exp 2 introduces a calibrated judge supplying pair weights and an abstention-aware data stream; Exp 3 integrates the full on-policy loop with baselines.
- Reuse the same tokenizer/model loading, optimizer, gradient checkpointing, and logging scaffolding.
- Ensure experiments are independent in their claims: Exp 1 isolates optimization stability; Exp 2 isolates the self-judge calibration and label efficiency; Exp 3 demonstrates end-to-end efficacy and efficiency vs baselines.

Reliability enhancements
- 3 seeds per configuration; bootstrap 95% CIs.
- Early stopping on val LC-win; save top-k checkpoints and report variance.
- Sanity checks: monitor EMA distance to actor LoRA, KL to SFT base, and ratio p99. If any exceed safety bounds (e.g., EMA distance > 4× median, KL > 0.2), trigger early rollback to last stable checkpoint and lower learning rate by ×0.8.
- Safety prefilter: run detoxify or a similar lightweight classifier to drop unsafe generations from pseudo-labels.
- OOD guard: drop pairs where SFT base log-prob is extremely low (ood_logprob_thresh) to avoid off-manifold drift.

What to log (per our metrics)
- Stability: per-step DPO loss, gradient norm, p99 |Δ|, collapse counters, NaNs.
- Behavior: average output length, entropy, repetition (unique n-gram ratio), KL to SFT.
- Judge: AUROC, ECE, coverage vs target, length-bucket bias, abstention rate.
- Efficiency: tokens/sec, VRAM peak, wall-clock/round, human labels consumed.

Ablation toggles (one at a time)
- EMA off; adaptive ε/β off (use tuned εfixed); Huberization off; LoftQ off; judge abstention off; length normalization off; safety gate off; dual KL off.

Expected results summary (what should happen if hypotheses hold)
- Exp 1: QA-DPO (M4) shows substantially reduced loss variance and gradient spikes, fewer collapses, controlled verbosity, and better convergence than M1–M3; LoftQ provides an additional margin of stability.
- Exp 2: Calibrated judge meets coverage/accuracy targets, cuts verbosity bias, and the actor trained on confident pseudo-pairs + a small human trickle outperforms both naive self-rewarding and human-only DPO at the same label budget.
- Exp 3: End-to-end qSR-DPO matches PPO-level stability and near-PPO quality while being faster, lighter (no RM), and more label-efficient, and decisively outperforms static/self-rewarding baselines in quality and stability.

Notes on LoftQ practicality
- If you have an official LoftQ implementation, use it to pre-initialize LoRA residuals. Otherwise, emulate its spirit by computing per-layer SVD low-rank residuals on dequantized weights for initialization statistics and use those residual norms to scale layer-wise learning rates. This preserves most benefits (better adapter alignment to quantized subspace) without bespoke code.

Closing
These experiments collectively validate the quantization-aware, self-rewarded DPO pipeline on a single GPU. The provided code sketches are designed to run with widely-used libraries, minimize bespoke implementations, and expose all toggles needed for comprehensive ablations and robust, reproducible conclusions.

def set_seed(seed: int = 42):
    random.seed(seed)

class SimpleTokenizer:
    """Fallback tiny word-level tokenizer if HF is unavailable."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.vocab = {"<pad>":0, "<eos>":1}
        self.inv_vocab = {0:"<pad>", 1:"<eos>"}
    def build(self, texts: List[str]):
        for t in texts:
            for w in t.lower().split():
                if w not in self.vocab:
                    idx = len(self.vocab)
                    self.vocab[w] = idx
                    self.inv_vocab[idx] = w
    def __call__(self, text: str, return_tensors: Optional[str] = None):
        ids = [self.vocab.get(w, 1) for w in text.lower().split()] + [1]
        attn = [1]*len(ids)
        if return_tensors == "pt":
            return {"input_ids": torch.tensor([ids], dtype=torch.long), "attention_mask": torch.tensor([attn], dtype=torch.long)}
        return {"input_ids": ids, "attention_mask": attn}
    def decode(self, ids, skip_special_tokens=True):
        if isinstance(ids, (list, np.ndarray)):
            return " ".join([self.inv_vocab.get(int(i), "?") for i in ids])
        else:
            return " ".join([self.inv_vocab.get(int(i), "?") for i in ids.tolist()])
    @property
    def eos_token_id(self):
        return 1

class TinyLM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size=2048, d_model=256, n_layers=2, n_heads=4):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(d_model=d_model, nhead=n_heads, dim_feedforward=4*d_model, batch_first=True)
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=n_layers)
        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.lm_head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask=None):
        x = self.embed(input_ids)
        if attention_mask is not None:
            # convert mask to key_padding_mask (True means to ignore)
            kpm = attention_mask == 0
        else:
            kpm = None
        x = self.encoder(x, src_key_padding_mask=kpm)
        x = self.ln(x)
        logits = self.lm_head(x)
        return type("Out", (), {"logits": logits})
    def generate(self, input_ids, attention_mask=None, max_new_tokens=64, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9):
        # Greedy + nucleus sampling naive implementation
        self.eval()
        ids = input_ids.clone()
        device = ids.device
        for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
            out = self.forward(ids, attention_mask)
            logits = out.logits[:, -1, :] / max(1e-6, temperature)
            # nucleus sampling
            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            sorted_probs, sorted_idx = torch.sort(probs, descending=True)
            cumulative = torch.cumsum(sorted_probs, dim=-1)
            cutoff = cumulative > top_p
            cutoff[:, 0] = False
            sorted_probs[cutoff] = 0
            sorted_probs = sorted_probs / (sorted_probs.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8)
            next_idx = torch.multinomial(sorted_probs, num_samples=1)
            next_token = sorted_idx.gather(-1, next_idx)
            ids = torch.cat([ids, next_token], dim=1)
            if next_token.item() == 1:  # eos
                break
        return ids

@dataclass
class PairItem:
    prompt: str
    chosen: str
    rejected: str
    weight: float = 1.0

class SyntheticPreferenceDataset(Dataset):
    """Create synthetic preference pairs with multiple patterns to test robustness.
    Patterns:
      - balanced: labels are consistent without verbosity bias
      - verbose_bias: chosen responses tend to be longer
      - noise_heavy: some label flips (noisy preferences)
    """
    def __init__(self, n: int, pattern: str = "balanced", seed: int = 0):
        super().__init__()
        set_seed(seed)
        self.items: List[PairItem] = []
        topics = [
            ("Explain photosynthesis.",
             "Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert light into chemical energy, producing glucose and oxygen.",
             "Plants like light."),
            ("What is the capital of France?",
             "The capital of France is Paris.",
             "France is a country in Europe."),
            ("Give two benefits of exercise.",
             "Exercise improves cardiovascular health and enhances mental well-being.",
             "Exercise is sometimes good."),
            ("Summarize the water cycle.",
             "Water evaporates, condenses into clouds, and precipitates, cycling through reservoirs.",
             "Rain happens.")
        ]
        for i in range(n):
            p, good, bad = random.choice(topics)
            if pattern == "balanced":
                chosen, rejected = good, bad
            elif pattern == "verbose_bias":
                # Ensure chosen is longer; sometimes extend verbosity
                chosen = good + " This process involves multiple steps and feedback mechanisms that maintain balance in ecosystems."
                rejected = bad
            elif pattern == "noise_heavy":
                # 30% chance of flipping to inject noise
                if random.random() < 0.3:
                    chosen, rejected = bad, good
                else:
                    chosen, rejected = good, bad
            else:
                chosen, rejected = good, bad
            self.items.append(PairItem(p, chosen, rejected, weight=1.0))
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)
    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        it = self.items[idx]
        return {"prompt": it.prompt, "chosen": it.chosen, "rejected": it.rejected, "weight": it.weight}


def concat_datasets(ds_list: List[SyntheticPreferenceDataset]):
    items = []
    for ds in ds_list:
        items.extend(ds.items)
    out = SyntheticPreferenceDataset(0)
    out.items = items
    return out


# --------------------------
# Build inputs and masks for DPO
# --------------------------

def build_lm_inputs(tokenizer, prompt: str, response: str, max_length=256, device="cpu"):
    # pack as [prompt + response], mask marking only response tokens
    if HF_AVAILABLE and hasattr(tokenizer, "apply_chat_template"):
        # Use generic fallback prompt formatting
        text = prompt + "\n\n" + response
    else:
        text = prompt + "\n\n" + response
    enc_prompt = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")
    enc_all = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt")
    input_ids = enc_all["input_ids"][:, :max_length].to(device)
    attention_mask = enc_all["attention_mask"][:, :max_length].to(device)

    # response start index
    resp_start = enc_prompt["input_ids"].shape[1]
    resp_len = input_ids.shape[1] - resp_start
    resp_mask = torch.zeros_like(input_ids)
    resp_mask[:, resp_start:] = 1

    # labels for LM; we will compute next-token log probs; fill -100 for ignore
    labels = input_ids.clone()
    labels[attention_mask == 0] = -100
    return {
        "input_ids": input_ids,
        "attention_mask": attention_mask,
        "labels": labels,
        "response_mask": resp_mask,
    }


def collate_pairs(batch: List[Dict], tokenizer, max_length=256, device="cpu"):
    # returns dict with tensors for chosen/rejected packed separately
    chosen_inputs = {"input_ids": [], "attention_mask": [], "labels": [], "response_mask": []}
    rejected_inputs = {"input_ids": [], "attention_mask": [], "labels": [], "response_mask": []}
    weights = []
    for ex in batch:
        ci = build_lm_inputs(tokenizer, ex["prompt"], ex["chosen"], max_length, device)
        ri = build_lm_inputs(tokenizer, ex["prompt"], ex["rejected"], max_length, device)
        for k in chosen_inputs:
            chosen_inputs[k].append(ci[k])
            rejected_inputs[k].append(ri[k])
        weights.append(ex.get("weight", 1.0))
    for k in chosen_inputs:
        chosen_inputs[k] = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_sequence(chosen_inputs[k], batch_first=True, padding_value=0)
        rejected_inputs[k] = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_sequence(rejected_inputs[k], batch_first=True, padding_value=0)
    return {
        "chosen_inputs": chosen_inputs,
        "rejected_inputs": rejected_inputs,
        "pair_weight": torch.tensor(weights, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    }


# --------------------------
# Log-probs and QA-DPO loss
# --------------------------

def token_logps_from_logits(logits: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor):
    # logits: (B, T, V), labels: (B, T)
    logps = F.log_softmax(logits[:, :-1, :], dim=-1)
    lbls = labels[:, 1:].clone()
    lbls[lbls < 0] = 0
    tok_logp = torch.gather(logps, -1, lbls.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
    return tok_logp


def length_normalize(logps: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, eps=1e-8):
    return (logps * mask).sum(-1) / (mask.sum(-1) + eps)


def huber_weight(z, delta=1.0):
    return delta / (delta + z.abs())


def qa_dpo_loss(
    logp_actor_pos, logp_actor_neg,
    logp_ref_pos, logp_ref_neg,
    mask_pos, mask_neg,
    eps_token: float, beta: float,
    tie_margin: float = 0.0, huber_delta: float = 1.0,
    pair_weight: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
):
    dpos = (logp_actor_pos - logp_ref_pos).clamp(-eps_token, eps_token)
    dneg = (logp_actor_neg - logp_ref_neg).clamp(-eps_token, eps_token)
    s_pos = length_normalize(dpos, mask_pos)
    s_neg = length_normalize(dneg, mask_neg)
    z = beta * ((s_pos - s_neg) - tie_margin)
    w = huber_weight(z, delta=huber_delta)
    if pair_weight is not None:
        w = w * pair_weight
    loss = -torch.log(torch.sigmoid(z) + 1e-8)
    ratio_vals = torch.cat([(dpos.abs()*mask_pos).reshape(-1), (dneg.abs()*mask_neg).reshape(-1)], dim=0)
    ratio_vals = ratio_vals[ratio_vals > 0]
    ratio_p99 = torch.quantile(ratio_vals, 0.99).item() if ratio_vals.numel() > 0 else 0.0
    return (w * loss).mean(), {
        "z_mean": z.mean().item(),
        "w_mean": w.mean().item(),
        "ratio_p99": ratio_p99,
    }


# --------------------------
# EMA reference (full-parameter fallback)
# --------------------------

class FullEMA:
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, tau: float = 0.995, device: str = "cpu"):
        self.tau = tau
        self.shadow = {k: v.detach().clone().to(device) for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
        self.device = device
    @torch.no_grad()
    def update(self, model: nn.Module):
        for k, v in model.state_dict().items():
            self.shadow[k].mul_(self.tau).add_(v.detach().to(self.device), alpha=1.0 - self.tau)
    @torch.no_grad()
    def swap_in(self, model: nn.Module):
        backup = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
        model.load_state_dict(self.shadow, strict=False)
        return backup
    @torch.no_grad()
    def swap_back(self, model: nn.Module, backup: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]):
        model.load_state_dict(backup, strict=False)


# --------------------------
# Sigma estimator (robust MAD)
# --------------------------

from collections import deque
class SigmaQEstimator:
    def __init__(self, window_tokens=200_000):
        self.window = deque(maxlen=window_tokens)
        self._mad_c = 1.4826
    @torch.no_grad()
    def update_with_batch(self, token_deltas: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor):
        vals = token_deltas[mask.bool()].detach().float().cpu().tolist()
        self.window.extend(vals)
    def sigma(self):
        if len(self.window) < 100:
            return 0.05
        arr = np.array(self.window)
        med = np.median(arr)
        mad = np.median(np.abs(arr - med))
        return float(self._mad_c * mad)
    def epsilon_beta(self, k=2.0, beta_floor=0.1, beta_cap=2.0):
        s = max(self.sigma(), 1e-4)
        eps = k * s
        beta = min(beta_cap, max(beta_floor, 1.0 / s))
        return eps, beta

@dataclass
class TrainConfig:
    method: str  # 'vanilla', 'fixed_clip', 'ema_fixed', 'qa_dpo'
    fixed_eps: float = 0.2
    epochs: int = 1
    steps_per_epoch: int = 50
    batch_size: int = 4
    lr: float = 1e-4
    beta_floor: float = 0.1
    beta_cap: float = 2.0
    k_eps: float = 2.0
    huber_delta: float = 1.0
    tie_margin: float = 0.0
    ema_tau: float = 0.995
    print_every: int = 10
    max_length: int = 256
    device: str = "cpu"


def get_model_and_tokenizer(fast_test=True, device="cpu"):
    if HF_AVAILABLE:
        model_name = "sshleifer/tiny-gpt2" if fast_test else "sshleifer/tiny-gpt2"
        tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
        if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
            tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
        model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name)
        model.to(device)
        return model, tokenizer
    else:
        # build minimal tokenizer/model on the fly
        tok = SimpleTokenizer()
        # Build vocab from synthetic corpus
        texts = ["Explain photosynthesis.","What is the capital of France?","Give two benefits of exercise.","Summarize the water cycle."]
        texts += [
            "Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert light into chemical energy, producing glucose and oxygen.",
            "The capital of France is Paris.",
            "Exercise improves cardiovascular health and enhances mental well-being.",
            "Water evaporates, condenses into clouds, and precipitates, cycling through reservoirs.",
        ]
        tok.build(texts)
        model = TinyLM(vocab_size=len(tok.vocab))
        model.to(device)
        return model, tok


def compute_token_logps(model, inputs: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]):
    out = model(input_ids=inputs["input_ids"], attention_mask=inputs.get("attention_mask", None))
    tok_logp = token_logps_from_logits(out.logits, inputs["labels"])
    return tok_logp


def train_one_method(method_name: str,
                     model: nn.Module,
                     tokenizer,
                     train_loader: DataLoader,
                     val_loader: Optional[DataLoader],
                     cfg: TrainConfig,
                     base_model_for_kl: Optional[nn.Module] = None,
                     seed: int = 0):
    set_seed(seed)
    device = cfg.device
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=cfg.lr, weight_decay=0.01)
    ema = FullEMA(model, tau=cfg.ema_tau, device=device)
    sigma_est = SigmaQEstimator(window_tokens=100_000)
    static_ref = FullEMA(model, tau=1.0, device=device)  # snapshot at start

    losses = []
    grad_norms = []
    ratio_p99_hist = []
    sigma_hist = []

    print(f"[Train] Method={method_name} seed={seed} epochs={cfg.epochs} steps/epoch~{cfg.steps_per_epoch}")

    step = 0
    for ep in range(cfg.epochs):
        for batch in train_loader:
            model.train()
            step += 1
            collated = collate_pairs(batch, tokenizer, max_length=cfg.max_length, device=device)
            # Forward actor
            logp_actor_pos = compute_token_logps(model, collated["chosen_inputs"])  # (B,T-1)
            logp_actor_neg = compute_token_logps(model, collated["rejected_inputs"])  # (B,T-1)
            mask_pos = collated["chosen_inputs"]["response_mask"][:, 1:].to(logp_actor_pos.dtype)
            mask_neg = collated["rejected_inputs"]["response_mask"][:, 1:].to(logp_actor_neg.dtype)

            # Reference
            if method_name in ["vanilla", "fixed_clip"]:
                # use static ref
                backup = static_ref.swap_in(model)
                with torch.no_grad():
                    logp_ref_pos = compute_token_logps(model, collated["chosen_inputs"])
                    logp_ref_neg = compute_token_logps(model, collated["rejected_inputs"])
                static_ref.swap_back(model, backup)
                eps = cfg.fixed_eps if method_name == "fixed_clip" else 10.0  # effectively no clipping for vanilla
                beta = 1.0
            elif method_name in ["ema_fixed", "qa_dpo"]:
                backup = ema.swap_in(model)
                with torch.no_grad():
                    logp_ref_pos = compute_token_logps(model, collated["chosen_inputs"])
                    logp_ref_neg = compute_token_logps(model, collated["rejected_inputs"])
                ema.swap_back(model, backup)
                if method_name == "ema_fixed":
                    eps = cfg.fixed_eps
                    beta = 1.0
                else:
                    # update sigma estimator with deltas
                    with torch.no_grad():
                        sigma_est.update_with_batch(logp_actor_pos - logp_ref_pos, mask_pos)
                        sigma_est.update_with_batch(logp_actor_neg - logp_ref_neg, mask_neg)
                    eps, beta = sigma_est.epsilon_beta(k=cfg.k_eps, beta_floor=cfg.beta_floor, beta_cap=cfg.beta_cap)
            else:
                raise ValueError("Unknown method")

            loss_dpo, stats = qa_dpo_loss(
                logp_actor_pos, logp_actor_neg, logp_ref_pos, logp_ref_neg,
                mask_pos, mask_neg, eps_token=eps, beta=beta,
                tie_margin=cfg.tie_margin, huber_delta=cfg.huber_delta,
                pair_weight=collated["pair_weight"].to(logp_actor_pos.device)
            )
            loss = loss_dpo

            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
            opt.step()

            if method_name in ["ema_fixed", "qa_dpo"] and step % 10 == 0:
                ema.update(model)

            # logs
            with torch.no_grad():
                gn = 0.0
                for p in model.parameters():
                    if p.grad is not None:
                        gn += p.grad.data.norm(2).item() ** 2
                gn = math.sqrt(gn)
            losses.append(loss.item())
            grad_norms.append(gn)
            ratio_p99_hist.append(stats["ratio_p99"])
            if method_name == "qa_dpo":
                sigma_hist.append(sigma_est.sigma())

            if step % cfg.print_every == 0:
                print({
                    "ep": ep, "step": step, "loss": round(loss.item(), 4),
                    "grad_norm": round(gn, 4), "eps": round(eps, 4), "beta": round(beta, 4),
                    "ratio_p99": round(stats["ratio_p99"], 4),
                    "sigma": round(sigma_est.sigma(), 4) if method_name == "qa_dpo" else None,
                })

            if step >= cfg.steps_per_epoch:
                break
        if step >= cfg.steps_per_epoch:
            break

    history = {
        "loss": losses, "grad_norm": grad_norms,
        "ratio_p99": ratio_p99_hist, "sigma": sigma_hist,
    }
    return history


def plot_curves_curated(histories: Dict[str, Dict[str, List[float]]], out_prefix: str = "exp1"):
    # Training loss
    for metric in ["loss", "grad_norm", "ratio_p99", "sigma"]:
        plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
        for name, hist in histories.items():
            if metric not in hist or len(hist[metric]) == 0:
                continue
            plt.plot(hist[metric], label=name)
        plt.xlabel("Step")
        plt.ylabel(metric)
        plt.legend()
        fname = f"{metric}_{out_prefix}.pdf"
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(fname, bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close()
        print(f"Saved {fname}")

# Experiment 2: Judge with calibration and abstention
# --------------------------

class JudgeHead(nn.Module):
    """Small scalar scoring head on top of a frozen LM backbone.
    We take the last hidden from the LM logits' penultimate layer by reusing logits as proxy features
    if hidden states are unavailable (Tiny model). Otherwise, use average pooled embeddings from logits.
    """
    def __init__(self, d_in: int, hidden: int = 128):
        super().__init__()
        self.ff = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_in, hidden), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(hidden, 1)
        )
    def forward(self, feats: torch.Tensor):
        return self.ff(feats).squeeze(-1)


def sequence_feature_from_model(model: nn.Module, inputs: Dict[str, torch.Tensor], pool: str = "mean"):
    # Convert logits to features by averaging over sequence after softmax temperature (proxy)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = model(input_ids=inputs["input_ids"], attention_mask=inputs.get("attention_mask", None))
        logits = out.logits  # (B, T, V)
    probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
    # take mean over tokens, then top-k principal features via random projection to reduce dim
    mean_feat = probs.mean(dim=1)  # (B, V)
    return mean_feat  # high dim; judge head will reduce


def build_pair_features(model, tokenizer, batch: List[Dict], device="cpu", max_length=256):
    feats_a, feats_b, labels, lengths = [], [], [], []
    for ex in batch:
        a = build_lm_inputs(tokenizer, ex["prompt"], ex["chosen"], max_length, device)
        b = build_lm_inputs(tokenizer, ex["prompt"], ex["rejected"], max_length, device)
        fa = sequence_feature_from_model(model, a)
        fb = sequence_feature_from_model(model, b)
        feats_a.append(fa)
        feats_b.append(fb)
        labels.append(1.0)  # chosen preferred over rejected
        la = int(a["attention_mask"].sum().item())
        lb = int(b["attention_mask"].sum().item())
        lengths.append((la, lb))
    feats_a = torch.cat(feats_a, dim=0)
    feats_b = torch.cat(feats_b, dim=0)
    labels = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.float32, device=feats_a.device)
    return feats_a, feats_b, labels, lengths


def train_judge(model_lm: nn.Module, tokenizer, train_ds: Dataset, calib_ds: Dataset, device="cpu", max_length=256, steps=50, lr=5e-4):
    # Train a small judge head on top of LM-derived features
    # Prepare a small random projection to reduce V dimension
    dummy = build_lm_inputs(tokenizer, "prompt", "response", max_length, device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = model_lm(input_ids=dummy["input_ids"], attention_mask=dummy["attention_mask"])
    V = out.logits.shape[-1]
    proj = nn.Linear(V, 128, bias=False).to(device)
    nn.init.normal_(proj.weight, std=0.02)

    judge = JudgeHead(d_in=128).to(device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(list(judge.parameters()) + list(proj.parameters()), lr=lr, weight_decay=0.01)

    dl = DataLoader(train_ds, batch_size=8, shuffle=True)
    for step in range(steps):
        batch = next(iter(dl))
        fa, fb, labels, _ = build_pair_features(model_lm, tokenizer, [batch[i] for i in range(len(batch["prompt"]))] if isinstance(batch["prompt"], list) else [batch], device)
        fa = proj(fa)
        fb = proj(fb)
        # margin score
        margin = judge(fa) - judge(fb)
        # light length normalization: penalize pref for much longer
        loss = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(margin, labels.to(margin.device))
        opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(judge.parameters(), 1.0)
        opt.step()
        if step % 10 == 0:
            print({"judge_step": step, "loss": round(loss.item(), 4)})

    # Calibration on calib set
    if not SKLEARN_AVAILABLE:
        print("scikit-learn not available; skipping full calibration.")
        return judge, proj, {"T": 1.0, "iso_x": np.array([0,1]), "iso_y": np.array([0,1]), "bin_thresholds": {"short":0.8, "med":0.8, "long":0.8}}

    # collect margins and labels (labels=1)
    calib_dl = DataLoader(calib_ds, batch_size=16, shuffle=False)
    margins, y, lengths = [], [], []
    for batch in calib_dl:
        exs = [batch[i] for i in range(len(batch["prompt"]))] if isinstance(batch["prompt"], list) else [batch]
        fa, fb, labels_true, lens = build_pair_features(model_lm, tokenizer, exs, device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            fa = proj(fa)
            fb = proj(fb)
            m = (judge(fa) - judge(fb)).detach().cpu().numpy()
        margins.append(m)
        y.extend([1]*len(m))  # chosen vs rejected are gold
        for la, lb in lens:
            lengths.append(max(la, lb))
    margins = np.concatenate(margins) if len(margins) > 0 else np.array([0.0])
    y = np.array(y)
    lengths = np.array(lengths)

    # Temperature scaling to minimize NLL
    def nll_T(T):
        p = 1.0/(1.0 + np.exp(-margins/max(T, 1e-3)))
        eps = 1e-8
        return -np.mean(y*np.log(p+eps) + (1-y)*np.log(1-p+eps))

    T_grid = np.linspace(0.1, 5.0, 50)
    T_hat = T_grid[np.argmin([nll_T(T) for T in T_grid])]
    probs_T = 1.0/(1.0 + np.exp(-margins/max(T_hat,1e-3)))

    iso = IsotonicRegression(y_min=0.0, y_max=1.0, increasing=True) if SKLEARN_AVAILABLE else None
    if SKLEARN_AVAILABLE:
        calib_p = iso.fit_transform(probs_T, y)
    else:
        calib_p = probs_T

    # Conformal thresholds per length bin
    bins = {"short": (0,128), "med": (128,256), "long": (256,9999)}
    thresholds = {}
    for name, (lo, hi) in bins.items():
        idx = (lengths>=lo) & (lengths<hi)
        if idx.sum() < 10:
            thresholds[name] = 0.8
            continue
        nc = 1.0 - np.where(y[idx]==1, calib_p[idx], 1.0-calib_p[idx])
        alpha = 0.1
        q = np.quantile(nc, 1-alpha)
        thresholds[name] = float(1.0 - q)

    calib_artifacts = {
        "T": float(T_hat),
        "iso_x": iso.X_thresholds_ if SKLEARN_AVAILABLE else np.array([0.0, 1.0]),
        "iso_y": iso.y_thresholds_ if SKLEARN_AVAILABLE else np.array([0.0, 1.0]),
        "bin_thresholds": thresholds
    }
    print({"judge_calibration_T": round(T_hat,3), "bin_thresholds": thresholds})
    return judge, proj, calib_artifacts


def calibrated_prob_from_margin(margin: float, T: float, iso_x: np.ndarray, iso_y: np.ndarray):
    pT = 1.0/(1.0 + math.exp(-margin/max(T,1e-3)))
    # piecewise-linear interp via numpy
    return float(np.interp(pT, iso_x, iso_y))


def generate_pseudo_pairs(actor_model, tokenizer, prompts: List[str], judge: JudgeHead, proj: nn.Linear, calib: Dict, device="cpu"):
    accepted = []
    abstained = 0
    for prompt in prompts:
        # generate k candidates with diverse decoding
        inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")
        if isinstance(inputs["input_ids"], list):
            inputs = {k: torch.tensor([v], dtype=torch.long, device=device) for k,v in inputs.items()}
        else:
            inputs = {k: v.to(device) for k,v in inputs.items()}
        cands = []
        for temp, top_p in [(0.7,0.9), (0.9,0.95), (0.7,0.95)]:
            out_ids = actor_model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=32, temperature=temp, top_p=top_p)
            new_ids = out_ids[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:].detach().cpu().tolist()
            text = tokenizer.decode(new_ids, skip_special_tokens=True) if HF_AVAILABLE else tokenizer.decode(new_ids)
            cands.append(text)
        # pairwise scores
        for i in range(len(cands)):
            for j in range(i+1, len(cands)):
                a, b = cands[i], cands[j]
                a_in = build_lm_inputs(tokenizer, prompt, a, device=device)
                b_in = build_lm_inputs(tokenizer, prompt, b, device=device)
                with torch.no_grad():
                    fa = sequence_feature_from_model(actor_model, a_in)
                    fb = sequence_feature_from_model(actor_model, b_in)
                    fa = proj(fa)
                    fb = proj(fb)
                    margin = (judge(fa) - judge(fb)).item()
                # bin by length
                la = int(a_in["attention_mask"].sum().item())
                lb = int(b_in["attention_mask"].sum().item())
                length_bin = "short" if max(la,lb) < 128 else ("med" if max(la,lb) < 256 else "long")
                p_hat = calibrated_prob_from_margin(margin, calib["T"], calib["iso_x"], calib["iso_y"])
                thr = calib["bin_thresholds"][length_bin]
                if p_hat >= thr:
                    w = (2.0 * abs(p_hat - 0.5)) ** 1.0
                    accepted.append({"prompt": prompt, "chosen": a, "rejected": b, "weight": float(w)})
                elif (1.0-p_hat) >= thr:
                    w = (2.0 * abs((1.0-p_hat) - 0.5)) ** 1.0
                    accepted.append({"prompt": prompt, "chosen": b, "rejected": a, "weight": float(w)})
                else:
                    abstained += 1
    print({"pseudo_pairs": len(accepted), "abstained_pairs": abstained})
    ds = SyntheticPreferenceDataset(0)
    ds.items = [PairItem(**ex) for ex in accepted]
    return ds


def judge_eval(judge: JudgeHead, proj: nn.Linear, model_lm, tokenizer, eval_ds: Dataset, device="cpu", max_length=256):
    # Evaluate AUROC, confusion matrix at 0.5, ECE
    if not SKLEARN_AVAILABLE:
        print("scikit-learn not available; skipping judge eval.")
        return {"auroc": None, "ece": None}
    dl = DataLoader(eval_ds, batch_size=8, shuffle=False)
    y_true, y_prob = [], []
    for batch in dl:
        exs = [batch[i] for i in range(len(batch["prompt"]))] if isinstance(batch["prompt"], list) else [batch]
        fa, fb, labels_true, _ = build_pair_features(model_lm, tokenizer, exs, device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            fa = proj(fa); fb = proj(fb)
            m = (judge(fa) - judge(fb)).detach().cpu().numpy()
        p = 1.0/(1.0 + np.exp(-m))
        y_true.extend([1]*len(p))
        y_prob.extend(p.tolist())
    y_true = np.array(y_true); y_prob = np.array(y_prob)
    # confusion at 0.5 (labels are always 1 for chosen>rejected in this ds)
    y_pred = (y_prob >= 0.5).astype(int)
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred)
    plt.figure(figsize=(4,3))
    sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt="d", cmap="Blues")
    plt.title("Judge confusion matrix")
    plt.xlabel("Predicted"); plt.ylabel("True")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("confusion_matrix_judge.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()
    print("Saved confusion_matrix_judge.pdf")
    # AUROC
    auroc = roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob)
    # ECE
    bins = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 11)
    binids = np.digitize(y_prob, bins) - 1
    ece = 0.0
    for b in range(len(bins)-1):
        idx = binids == b
        if idx.sum() == 0:
            continue
        acc = np.mean((y_prob[idx]>=0.5)==y_true[idx])
        conf = np.mean(y_prob[idx])
        ece += (idx.sum()/len(y_prob))*abs(acc - conf)
    print({"judge_auroc": round(auroc,3), "judge_ece": round(ece,3)})
    return {"auroc": auroc, "ece": ece}

def on_policy_round(actor_model, tokenizer, seed_prompts: List[str], judge: JudgeHead, proj: nn.Linear, calib: Dict,
                    train_cfg: TrainConfig, rounds: int = 2, device="cpu"):
    histories = []
    for r in range(rounds):
        print(f"[On-Policy] Round {r+1}/{rounds}")
        # Generate pseudo-pairs
        pseudo_ds = generate_pseudo_pairs(actor_model, tokenizer, seed_prompts, judge, proj, calib, device=device)
        # Mix with a small human pool (here reuse a small balanced ds as proxy)
        human_ds = SyntheticPreferenceDataset(n=20, pattern="balanced", seed=r)
        mixed = concat_datasets([pseudo_ds, human_ds])
        dl = DataLoader(mixed, batch_size=train_cfg.batch_size, shuffle=True)
        # Train QA-DPO a few steps
        hist = train_one_method("qa_dpo", actor_model, tokenizer, dl, None, train_cfg, seed=r)
        histories.append(hist)
    # Plot acceptance and loss curve
    # For simplicity, plot last round loss
    if len(histories) > 0:
        plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
        plt.plot(histories[-1]["loss"], label="qSR-DPO")
        plt.xlabel("Step"); plt.ylabel("loss")
        plt.legend(); plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig("training_loss_qsr-dpo.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close()
        print("Saved training_loss_qsr-dpo.pdf")
    return histories
